mcq.q: An economy has private consumption ₹600 crore, investment ₹200 crore, government purchases ₹150 crore, exports ₹80 crore and imports ₹100 crore. GDP at market prices is:
mcq.explain: By the expenditure method, add consumption (600), investment (200) and government purchases (150), and then net exports (80 − 100 = −20): the total is ₹930 crore. Net exports are negative here because imports exceed exports. Adding imports instead of subtracting them gives the wrong figure of ₹1,130 crore.
mcq.fast: GDPmp = C + I + G + (X − M); imports are subtracted.

mcq.q: GDP at market prices is ₹1,000 crore, depreciation ₹100 crore, net factor income from abroad −₹20 crore, indirect taxes ₹120 crore and subsidies ₹20 crore. National income (NNP at factor cost) is:
mcq.explain: NNP at factor cost = GDPmp − depreciation + NFIA − (indirect taxes − subsidies) = 1,000 − 100 + (−20) − (120 − 20) = ₹780 crore. Remember that net indirect taxes are deducted to move from market prices to factor cost, and a negative NFIA reduces the figure.

mcq.q: A farmer grows wheat worth ₹100 (no purchased inputs), a miller turns it into flour sold for ₹160, and a baker sells bread made from it for ₹250. The contribution of this chain to GDP is:
mcq.explain: Value added at each stage: farmer ₹100, miller ₹160 − ₹100 = ₹60, baker ₹250 − ₹160 = ₹90. Total value added = ₹250, which equals the value of the final good, bread. Adding all sales (₹510) would count the wheat and flour more than once — the problem of double counting.
mcq.fast: Sum of value added = value of final goods; never add all sales.

mcq.q: Nominal GDP is ₹1,200 lakh crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹1,000 lakh crore. The GDP deflator is:
mcq.explain: GDP deflator = (nominal GDP ÷ real GDP) × 100 = (1,200 ÷ 1,000) × 100 = 120. It shows that the general price level of all goods and services in GDP is 20% higher than in the base year. 83.33 inverts the ratio, and 20 is only the percentage rise.
mcq.topic: GDP — nominal, real and the GDP deflator

mcq.q: Nominal GDP of a year is ₹1,500 crore and the GDP deflator is 125. Real GDP is:
mcq.explain: Real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ deflator × 100 = 1,500 ÷ 125 × 100 = ₹1,200 crore. Real GDP removes the effect of price changes, so it is lower than nominal GDP when prices have risen since the base year. Multiplying instead of dividing gives the wrong ₹1,875 crore.
mcq.topic: GDP — nominal, real and the GDP deflator

mcq.q: Which of these is included while estimating national income?
options: Old-age pension paid by the government
mcq.explain: National income counts the value of current production of goods and services. Owner-occupied houses provide housing services, so an imputed rent is included. Pensions and scholarships are transfer payments with no current production in return, and sale of a used car is a transfer of an old asset, so all three are excluded.
mcq.topic: GDP and welfare; limitations of national income computation
mcq.fast: Included: current production (even imputed). Excluded: transfers, second-hand sales.

mcq.q: A person buys shares worth ₹1,00,000 through a broker and pays a brokerage of ₹500. What is included in national income?
mcq.explain: Buying shares is a financial transaction that only transfers ownership of existing claims; it creates no new goods or services, so ₹1,00,000 is excluded. The broker's commission, however, is payment for a current service and is included in national income.
mcq.topic: GDP and welfare; limitations of national income computation
mcq.fast: Financial transactions out; the service fee (brokerage) in.

mcq.q: Compensation of employees ₹500 crore, rent ₹60 crore, interest ₹40 crore, profit ₹150 crore and mixed income of the self-employed ₹100 crore. Net domestic product at factor cost (income method) is:
mcq.explain: By the income method, add wages and salaries (compensation of employees, 500), the operating surplus made up of rent, interest and profit (60 + 40 + 150), and the mixed income of the self-employed (100): NDP at factor cost is ₹850 crore. Leaving out mixed income would understate it at ₹750 crore.
mcq.fast: Income method = CoE + rent + interest + profit + mixed income.

mcq.q: GVA at factor cost of an economy is ₹900 crore, production taxes are ₹30 crore and production subsidies ₹10 crore. GVA at basic prices is:
mcq.explain: GVA at basic prices = GVA at factor cost + production taxes − production subsidies = 900 + 30 − 10 = ₹920 crore. Product taxes and subsidies are added and subtracted only when moving further from basic prices to market prices.
mcq.topic: Market price, factor cost and basic price
mcq.fast: Basic prices = factor cost + production taxes − production subsidies.

mcq.q: Residents of a country earn ₹300 crore of factor income abroad, and non-residents earn ₹350 crore of factor income inside the country. Net factor income from abroad (in ₹ crore) is:
mcq.explain: NFIA = factor income earned by residents from abroad − factor income earned by non-residents in the domestic territory = 300 − 350 = −₹50 crore. Since NFIA is negative, the country's GNP is smaller than its GDP by ₹50 crore.
mcq.topic: Gross vs net, domestic vs national
mcq.fast: NFIA = earned abroad by residents − earned here by non-residents.

mcq.q: National income of a country is ₹2,00,000 crore and its population is 50 crore. Per capita income is:
mcq.explain: Per capita income = national income ÷ population = ₹2,00,000 crore ÷ 50 crore = ₹4,000 per person. The "crore" cancels out, so do not add zeros. Per capita income is a rough indicator of the average standard of living.
mcq.fast: Per capita = NI ÷ population (crore cancels crore).

mcq.q: In India, official national income estimates are compiled by the:
options: National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
mcq.explain: National accounts statistics in India are prepared by the National Statistical Office, which functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The RBI, NITI Aayog and the Finance Commission use these estimates, but they do not compile the official national income figures.
mcq.topic: National income accounting — meaning, who compiles it, why it matters

mcq.q: The value of household work done by home-makers for their own families is not included in national income. As a result, national income:
options: Understates the true value of production and welfare
mcq.explain: Non-market activities such as cooking, cleaning and caring by home-makers produce real value but have no market price, so they are left out of national income. This is one limitation of national income as a welfare measure: it understates the true production of the economy.
mcq.topic: GDP and welfare; limitations of national income computation
mcq.fast: Unpaid home work left out -> NI understates welfare.
